what_it_does: Federated learning (FL) is a privacy-preserving training approach where each user trains an AI model locally on their own device and only shares updates — never raw data — with a central server. For recommendation systems (like a streaming service suggesting movies), each user only looks up a tiny fraction of a huge table of learned embeddings (dense numerical representations of items); hiding which entries a user accessed is important for privacy. Oblivious RAM (ORAM) is a cryptographic technique that makes memory access patterns look random to an observer, hiding which rows were looked up. Existing ORAM approaches are too slow and wear out solid-state drives (SSDs — flash-based storage) too quickly to be practical at scale. FEDORA moves the ORAM data structure onto SSDs (which are far cheaper and larger than main memory chips) and optimizes access patterns to reduce the number of write operations that degrade SSD lifetime. It also introduces a formal privacy trade-off called epsilon-FDP (a tunable privacy budget similar in spirit to differential privacy) that lets operators accept a small, mathematically bounded privacy cost in exchange for far fewer ORAM operations, making the system fast enough for real deployments.
